paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss Ratio FLOPs
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the loss ratio (as a percentage) of different LLM configurations as a function of total floating-point operations (TFLOPs), comparing “Vanilla” LLM performance against various SepLLM variants. The x-axis, labeled “TFLOPs,” spans from 1e7 to 9e8 on a logarithmic scale, with tick marks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, 1e9, 2e9, 5e9, and 9e9 (though only up to 9e8 is shown), marked at intervals of 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, and 9e8. The y-axis, labeled “Loss Ratio (%)”, ranges from 94% to 100% on a linear scale, with tick marks at 94, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, and 100. The “Vanilla” configuration (purple triangles, solid line) remains nearly flat near 100% across all TFLOPs. The “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange squares, solid line) starts at ~98.2% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to ~100.2% at 4e8 TFLOPs, then stabilizes near 100%. “SepLLM (n=128)” (blue X’s, solid line) begins at ~97.2% at 1e7 TFLOPs, climbs to ~99.8% by 5e7 TFLOPs, and stays near 100% thereafter. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green diamonds, solid line) starts at ~97.5% at 1e7 TFLOPs, reaches ~100% by 5e7 TFLOPs, and fluctuates slightly around 100%. “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red circles, solid line) begins at 94% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises steeply to ~97.5% at 5e7 TFLOPs, then climbs gradually to ~98.8% by 9e8 TFLOPs, showing the lowest loss ratio among all SepLLM variants at lower TFLOPs but trailing behind others at higher TFLOPs.
